name: Pispa
overview: Pispa is a male figure from the tribe of Asher, identified uniquely as the son of Jether, also known as Ithran. The biblical record provides limited information about him beyond this paternal relationship. No additional notes or distinguishing attributes are given in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Pispa appears as a proper name in Scripture without an explicit meaning or divine origin indicated. It is recorded simply as Pispa in 1 Chronicles 7:38.
familyAndRelationships: Pispa is explicitly noted as the son of Ithran (Jether) according to 1 Chronicles 7:38. Scripture does not provide further family relationships or descendants associated with Pispa beyond this father-son connection.
scriptureSignificance: Pispa's significance lies primarily in his genealogical placement within the tribe of Asher, as documented in 1 Chronicles 7:38. His mention contributes to the biblical record of the descendants of Asher, preserving the lineage important for understanding the tribal history of Israel. Although no specific deeds or roles are attributed to him, his inclusion underscores the faithfulness of Scripture in recording God's chosen people and their families.
